concepts.title: Jacobian nullspace
concepts.description:
Local linear-algebra check on DF(x): a non-trivial null vector would indicate a first-order blind direction. For Nagata-type automorphisms the Jacobian determinant is constant and non-zero, so the nullspace is trivial everywhere — local invertibility does not by itself settle tameness or Jacobian-conjecture questions. Local gradient checks therefore cannot certify the global picture.

**Proof integrity** — evidence blobs are fingerprinted via evidence.algorithm + evidence.digest (primary sha3-256). See concept sha3-integrity. Tamper-*authentication* (HMAC/signing) is a separate, unimplemented lane.

concepts.title: Nagata map
concepts.description: The Nagata automorphism of affine 3-space: a polynomial automorphism with Jacobian determinant identically 1 that is wild (not tame). Often cited alongside the Jacobian conjecture; as an automorphism it is bijective, not a non-injective fiber counterexample. FactoryWager uses the name for related audit-graph edges (sample finding ↔ concepts).
references: Masayoshi Nagata — wild (non-tame) polynomial automorphism of A^3 with Jac ≡ 1
Jacobian conjecture (Keller) — open for dim ≥ 2; Nagata automorphism illustrates tameness vs Jacobian-determinant questions

concepts.title: SHA3 evidence integrity
concepts.description:
FactoryWager AuditFinding evidence blobs are fingerprinted with SHA3-256 via Bun.CryptoHasher('sha3-256'). SSOT catalog verify requires sha3-256; parse still accepts inbound sha256 for audit:migrate:sha3. Wire shape is evidence.algorithm + evidence.digest (Phase 2). This is tamper-detection only — keyed authentication (HMAC/signing) is a separate, unimplemented lane.

Bun shipped native SHA-3 support in v1.3.13 (WebCrypto SHA3-* + node:crypto / CryptoHasher). See relatedDocs SHA3-256 for the ship note.
